title: Stoke Space
summary: Washington company developing a fully reusable second stage, the part of a rocket most often thrown away.
bodyHtml:
Stoke Space is building a two-stage rocket whose second stage returns to Earth and lands, aiming at rapid and complete reuse rather than only booster recovery.

Its engine and heat-shield designs are aimed at aircraft-like turnaround, which is the main cost lever left after booster reuse.

Why it matters

  • Reusable second stage
  • Regeneratively cooled heat shield
  • Rapid turnaround target

businessMeaning: Booster reuse reset launch costs; second-stage reuse is the next step. The engineering problem is a heat shield that survives re-entry repeatedly.
investmentLens: Private; the read is through launch customers and materials suppliers.
